supersedes: program-v4 is a new question, not a revision of program-v2. It keeps v2's checkpoint, suite, task ids, seeds, phases, gates, statistics, agent and budgets, and replaces the memory score with a latency score. v2's nodes, scores and policies are not pooled with v4 and are not used as v4's starting point.

calibration.note: The same frozen unlabeled artifact program-v1 and program-v2 used; it carries no robot outcomes.

statistics.multiplicity: pre-register primary comparisons; report all others as exploratory

score.reference: uncompressed B16, four flow steps, stock execution path
score.formula: lower bound of the 95% interval of reference_median_observation_to_action_ms / candidate_median_observation_to_action_ms; both sides are timed in alternating blocks of the same evaluation, and the interval is a percentile cluster bootstrap over blocks
zero_unless: the smoke gate passes: successes >= gates.smoke_min_successes
the candidate's peak CUDA bytes are not above the reference's

starting_policy.note: The loop copies this default OptimalPolicy to policies/v000_initial/policy.py. The search starts with no trees, no beta sweeps and no scores: cycles/ and policies/ hold only what this run writes.

run_budget.note: Pre-registered launch budget. It matches the launch command in studies/program-v4/README.md; a run that changes it records the change in revisions.

starting_rules.rule: The score is the lower bound of the 95% interval of reference median observation-to-action latency divided by the candidate's, measured by the fixed evaluator in one process on frames collected from reference episodes, with a device synchronize before and after every timed select_action call, after warm-up, on observations never timed before. Both sides are timed in alternating blocks of the same evaluation, so a co-tenant burst lands in both; when a second reference does not fit beside the candidate, the reference is timed in blocks before compress and again after the candidate episodes and the two pools are combined. The interval is a percentile cluster bootstrap over blocks, so timing noise cannot create a win. The score is zero unless the smoke gate passes and the candidate's peak CUDA bytes are not above the reference's. The evaluator is evaluation/compression/solution.py with the latency module; a node never chooses its own measurement.

Failing conditions, recorded as guard_violation: a replaced clock or CUDA synchronizer; a stored or cached answer (reproducibility, order, select_action/predict_action_chunk agreement, observation sensitivity, novel-frame cost, physical arm-action error against the untouched policy on fresh frames, and the correlation of the arm change under a small pixel perturbation with the untouched policy's); work moved into reset; background or asynchronous work (episode wall time per step minus the policy's own time against the reference's); CPU or child-process work above the caps; new threads during timing; another process above a set share of the GPU during the timing blocks; an incomplete or drifting sandwich reference; peak CUDA bytes above the reference's. The discovery prompt states each one.

The policy-development agent gets read,write,edit,bash; repo source read-only at /tmp/repo without rsi/synth.py, GPU visible, network, writable /tmp/pkgs on PYTHONPATH, and a runnable replay.py in the workspace. It may run and measure its own replay before answering. The harness still audits, replays and selects; the agent's own numbers are never used.
1200 s per policy-development step, one repair attempt also after a not-better step.

Anytime. The prompt asks for a valid method.py early and in-place improvement after that. On timeout the harness audits and replays the file as it stands and records timeout_salvaged; it is accepted only if it passes the audit and strictly beats the incumbent. A missing or unusable file leaves status timeout. Cost and transcript are kept.

Live. The selected policy's plan_grid decides the next cycle's grid from the last three manifests and beta sweeps; the protocol grid values (max_parallelism, rounds_cap) and the run arguments (probe budget, GPU slots) are caps, and the protocol grid is the pre-registered fallback. A candidate whose plan_grid fails validation is rejected.

grid_plan.rationale: Pre-registered fallback grid and the caps on the policy's plan_grid. The live plan_grid chooses the applied grid within these caps.

dream_rsi.policy: paper-faithful replay policy; generated policy code must be recorded by hash
